A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same posterior-sampling research, despite the change from AdaPS to JAPS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration experiments, guidance ablations, robustness tests, and nonlinear deblurring results in Appendix B.1.

after.justification: v2 reports original linear and nonlinear restoration results in Tables 1–2, plus synthetic GMM experiments examining trained denoiser Jacobians in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The projection-based core and conditional DDIM formulation remain, but v2 changes the surrogate variance schedule from 1 - alpha_bar_t to (1 - alpha_bar_t)/sqrt(alpha_bar_t), introduces task-dependent lambda_t instead of v1’s fixed factor-two correction, and replaces the iterative scalar Gauss–Newton nonlinear extension with a locally linearized matrix solve (v1 Appendix B.1; v2 Section 3.5).

E1.justification: v2 adds box and random inpainting, HDR correction, and synthetic GMM training/analysis. Nonlinear deblurring expands from CelebA-HQ to ImageNet-256 as well; the CelebA-HQ experiment already existed in v1’s appendix. The original image datasets and super-resolution/deblurring coverage remain.

E2.justification: DAPS becomes an evaluated baseline, while DDRM and DDNM disappear from the main comparison. DiffPIR, DDPG, DPS, DSG, and ΠGDM remain. The retained CelebA-HQ nonlinear-deblurring comparison expands from DPS alone to DPS, DAPS, and ΠGDM equipped with the authors’ nonlinear extension (v2 Table 2).

E3.justification: v2 adds SSIM and FID to linear evaluation and SSIM to nonlinear evaluation. The surrogate ablation changes from 100 ImageNet super-resolution examples to 30 images across three tasks with a nine-value guidance-scale sweep. The GMM study introduces a new analytical-versus-trained evaluation protocol. The main 1,000-image, 100-step sampling setup remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds Jacobian symmetry/PSD diagnostics (Figure 2), replaces v1’s surrogate-pairing and fixed-scale ablation tables with five-candidate guidance comparisons across three tasks (Figure 3), and adds a JAPS/ΠGDM scale sweep (Figure 8). Noise, stochasticity, and step-count sensitivity analyses are substantially retained in Appendix C.

E5.justification: v1 reports point averages without dispersion estimates. v2 adds standard-deviation ellipsoids in Figure 1b and mean curves with standard deviations across 1,024 GMM samples in Figure 2. Its revised ablation explicitly uses a fixed seed. These disclosures do not establish increased independent runs or benchmark confidence intervals.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive task and metric results and replaces the AdaPS variant rows with JAPS results under revised guidance; dedicated noiseless-SR table entries disappear. Existing baseline numbers also change: DDPG’s noisy ImageNet SR LPIPS changes from 0.354 to 0.302, with PSNR remaining 25.55. ΠGDM’s ImageNet SR/Gaussian PSNR-LPIPS pairs exchange columns without explanation. These are reported changes, not established uniform performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds the exact likelihood-score/posterior-mean identity and proof (Proposition 3.1), a covariance–Jacobian identity with derivation (Appendix A.5), and a new nonlinear linearization derivation. The linear-Gaussian MAP calculation largely survives, while v1’s scalar-curvature Gauss–Newton derivation is replaced.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds hyperparameter-free, task-agnostic guidance scaling. v2 foregrounds bridging direct and proximal samplers, diagnosing trained-Jacobian non-idealities, and nonlinear restoration, and claims the first analysis of Jacobian non-ideality in this setting. DDIM scalability and the perception–distortion balance remain central claims.

C2.justification: v1 describes Jacobian-free magnitude estimation as an efficiency/stability compromise involving theoretically inexact omission. v2 instead interprets the Jacobian as covariance-based preconditioning and attributes harmful guidance to training-induced symmetry/PSD violations. It also treats adaptation to flow models as future work, whereas v1 described its construction as future-compatible with such samplers. The latent-diffusion limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents task/dataset-specific guidance values, DDPG inpainting hyperparameters, implementation choices for all six baselines, and the GMM model’s architecture and training recipe. Conversely, v1’s per-image runtime table and NVIDIA L40S hardware disclosure disappear. Both versions still promise code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from adaptive guidance scaling to bridging direct/proximal approaches through Jacobian analysis, including a new first-analysis novelty claim. v2 adds higher-order-gradient, covariance, latent-diffusion, and flow-model references, including Meng et al. and Bishop. Earlier connections to Li and Wang’s sampler and DreamFusion’s Jacobian omission are removed.

P1.justification: The title, method name, abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method narrative is reorganized around direct/proximal coupling and Jacobian analysis; DDIM reformulation moves later, and nonlinear development moves into the main text. Appendices are reorganized into proofs, method details, results, implementation details, and visual results.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The overview schematic is redrawn and combined with an averaged-performance plot, tables are reorganized to accommodate additional tasks and metrics, and new diagnostic and ablation plots appear. Qualitative comparisons are extensively redesigned as task-specific grids in Appendix E; retained sensitivity figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central method’s justification through the posterior-mean identity, covariance analysis, and analytical-versus-trained Jacobian diagnostics. Scale-controlled ablations and expanded nonlinear comparisons better test the proposed guidance, while Appendix D improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed runtime evidence and remaining reporting problems, particularly the conclusion’s tuning-free claim despite task-specific hyperparameters and unexplained baseline-value changes. The improvement rests on stronger reasoning and experimental support, rather than assumed across-version performance gains.
